# Problem 1: YouTube vs. lectures {.section-slide}

Confidence intervals and the t-test.

## Problem 1: the question

::: {.box}
We want to understand how students use social media. Today: **how much time do students spend on YouTube per day?**
:::

. . .

::: {.cards}
::: {.box .c}
<span class="tag">What we know</span>
A student attends on average **2 lectures a day**, 75 minutes each:
$$2\times 75=150 \text{ minutes}$$
:::
::: {.box .c}
<span class="tag">What we suspect</span>
Students spend **more** time on YouTube than in lectures.
:::
:::

. . .

::: {.box .key}
<span class="tag">Question</span>
Is the average daily YouTube time of students **more than 150 minutes**?
:::

. . .

::: {.box}
We cannot ask every student. We have to learn about all of them from a few.
:::

## The setup

| Object | In our problem |
|:--|:--|
| **Population** | All students at the university |
| **Variable** $X$ | A student's average daily YouTube time over the last week (minutes) |
| **Parameter** $\mu=E[X]$ | The mean of $X$ in the population: **unknown** |
| $\sigma=SD(X)$ | The standard deviation in the population: **also unknown** |
| **Benchmark** $\mu_0$ | $150$ minutes of lectures per day: a known number |

. . .

::: {.box .key}
We compare the unknown $\mu$ with the known benchmark $\mu_0=150$.
:::

## Our random sample

::: {.box}
We pick $n=16$ students **at random** from the list of all students. Each one opens the screen-time report on their phone and gives the daily YouTube average for last week. All 16 answer.
:::

<svg id="p1a-svg" viewBox="0 0 900 390" class="famplot" style="max-height:390px"></svg>

::: {.cap}
Classroom simulation: computer-generated data, not a real survey.
:::

  function dot(i, x, col) { return '<circle cx="' + cx(i) + '" cy="' + py(x) + '" r="7" fill="' + col + '"/>'; }
  function devs() {
    var d = "";
    X.forEach(function (x, i) {
      var c = x > 170 ? UP : DN;
      d += '<line x1="' + cx(i) + '" y1="' + py(170) + '" x2="' + cx(i) + '" y2="' + py(x) + '" stroke="' + c + '" stroke-width="5"/>' + dot(i, x, c);
    });
    return d;
  }
  function hline(v, col, dash) { return '<line x1="50" y1="' + py(v) + '" x2="812" y2="' + py(v) + '" stroke="' + col + '" stroke-width="3"' + (dash ? ' stroke-dasharray="8 5"' : '') + '/>'; }
  function frag(k, inner) { return '<g class="fragment" data-fragment-index="' + k + '">' + inner + '</g>'; }
  // one chart, two views: "data" and "mean"
  window.p1Chart = function (id, mode) {
    var g = "", v, top = "";
    for (v = 0; v <= 250; v += 50) g += '<line x1="50" y1="' + py(v) + '" x2="812" y2="' + py(v) + '" stroke="#e4e7eb"/><text x="42" y="' + (py(v) + 5) + '" text-anchor="end" font-size="14" fill="#7b8794">' + v + '</text>';
    g += text(8, 12, "minutes per day", "#7b8794", "start", 14);
    X.forEach(function (x, i) {
      g += '<line x1="' + cx(i) + '" y1="' + py(0) + '" x2="' + cx(i) + '" y2="' + py(x) + '" stroke="#d3d9e0" stroke-width="2"/>' + dot(i, x, "#2b6cb0");
      g += text(cx(i), 355, i + 1, "#7b8794", "middle", 14);
      top += text(cx(i), mode !== "data" && x < 170 ? py(x) + 24 : py(x) - 12, x, "#1f2933");
    });
    g += '<line x1="50" y1="' + py(0) + '" x2="812" y2="' + py(0) + '" stroke="#52606d" stroke-width="2"/>' + text(431, 380, "student", "#7b8794", "middle", 14);
    if (mode === "data") g += hline(150, "#c53030", true) + text(818, py(150) + 5, "lectures 150", "#c53030", "start", 15);
    if (mode === "mean") {

## What do we compute from the sample?

::: {.box}
Two numbers carry the information we need.
:::

::: {.cards}
::: {.box .key .c}
<span class="tag">Sample mean: the center</span>
$$\bar{X}=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^{n}X_i$$
:::
::: {.box .c}
<span class="tag">Sample SD: the spread</span>
$$s=\sqrt{\frac{1}{n-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\left(X_i-\bar{X}\right)^2}$$
:::
:::

. . .

::: {.box .good}
<span class="tag">The sample mean</span>
$$\bar{X}=\frac{235+199+\dots+187}{16}=\frac{2720}{16}=170 \text{ minutes}$$
:::

## The sample mean, visually

<svg id="p1m-svg" viewBox="0 0 900 390" class="famplot" style="max-height:445px"></svg>

<script>window.p1Chart("p1m-svg", "mean");</script>

::: {.fragment data-fragment-index="2"}
::: {.box .key}
$\bar{X}$ is the **balancing level**. The blue segments above it add up to 232 minutes, and so do the orange segments below it. So $\sum (X_i-\bar{X})=0$.
:::
:::

## The sample standard deviation

Deviations from $\bar{X}=170$ and their squares:

| $i$ | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 |
|:--|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|
| $X_i-170$ | $65$ | $29$ | $41$ | $-15$ | $40$ | $-23$ | $-82$ | $-79$ |
| squared | 4225 | 841 | 1681 | 225 | 1600 | 529 | 6724 | 6241 |

| $i$ | 9 | 10 | 11 | 12 | 13 | 14 | 15 | 16 |
|:--|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|
| $X_i-170$ | $-3$ | $6$ | $-1$ | $5$ | $-29$ | $2$ | $27$ | $17$ |
| squared | 9 | 36 | 1 | 25 | 841 | 4 | 729 | 289 |

. . .

::: {.box .good}
$$s^2=\frac{24000}{15}=1600,\qquad s=\sqrt{1600}=40 \text{ minutes}$$
:::

  function ends(step, x) {  // [start, tip] of student's segment, in pixels

    var d = x - 170;

    "We care about the <b>size</b> of a deviation, not its sign: <b>flip</b> the negative ones up.",
    "<b>Square</b> each one: (X<sub>i</sub> − X̄)². Signs disappear, and <b>large deviations grow the most</b>: 82 → 6724, but 5 → 25.",

  ];

  function L(y, col, dash, w) { return '<line x1="50" y1="' + y + '" x2="812" y2="' + y + '" stroke="' + col + '" stroke-width="' + (w || 3) + '"' + (dash ? ' stroke-dasharray="8 5"' : '') + '/>'; }
  var cur = 0, raf = null, guard = null;
  function frame(from, to, k) {

    var ticks = mode === "min" ? [0, 50, 100, 150, 200, 250] : mode === "abs" ? [0, 20, 40, 60, 80] : [0, 1000, 2000, 3000, 4000, 5000, 6000, 7000];
    ticks.forEach(function (t) {

    if (to === 5) g += '<rect x="50" y="' + py(210) + '" width="762" height="' + (py(130) - py(210)) + '" fill="' + GR + '" fill-opacity="' + (0.16 * k) + '"/>';
    var base0 = from < 2 || from === 5 ? py(170) : 335, base1 = to < 2 || to === 5 ? py(170) : 335, base = base0 + (base1 - base0) * k;
    X.forEach(function (x, i) {

      g += '<line x1="' + cx(i) + '" y1="' + y0 + '" x2="' + cx(i) + '" y2="' + y1 + '" stroke="' + col + '" stroke-width="5"/><circle cx="' + cx(i) + '" cy="' + y1 + '" r="7" fill="' + col + '"/>';

</script>

## Step 1: What is our best guess for $\mu$?

::: {.box}
<span class="tag">Theory</span>
We estimate the population mean by the sample mean: $\hat\mu=\bar{X}$.

- **Unbiased:** $E[\bar{X}]=\mu$.
- **Consistent:** $\bar{X}$ gets close to $\mu$ as $n$ grows.
:::

. . .

::: {.box .key}
<span class="tag">Our data</span>
$$\hat\mu=\bar{X}=170 \text{ minutes}$$
:::

. . .

::: {.box .warn}
170 is more than 150. But another 16 students would give another $\bar{X}$. **Could the gap of 20 minutes be just luck?**
:::

## Step 2: How precise is this guess?

::: {.box}
<span class="tag">Theory</span>
$\bar{X}$ varies from sample to sample, and $SD(\bar{X})=\dfrac{\sigma}{\sqrt n}$.

We do not know $\sigma$, so we replace it with $s$. This gives the **estimated standard error**:
$$SE=\frac{s}{\sqrt n}$$
:::

. . .

::: {.box .key}
<span class="tag">Our data</span>
$$SE=\frac{40}{\sqrt{16}}=10 \text{ minutes}$$
:::

. . .

::: {.box .good}
Roughly, 10 minutes is the typical size of the distance between $\bar{X}$ and $\mu$.
:::

## Step 3: Confidence interval (theory)

::: {.box}
If the population is **normal** and the sample is random, then
$$\frac{\bar{X}-\mu}{s/\sqrt n}\;\sim\; t_{n-1}$$
:::

. . .

::: {.box .key}
<span class="tag">$(1-\alpha)$ confidence interval for $\mu$</span>
$$\bar{X}\;\pm\; t_{\alpha/2,\,n-1}\,\frac{s}{\sqrt n}$$
:::

. . .

::: {.box .warn}
<span class="tag">What we assume</span>
**Random sample:** students chosen at random, and they all answer. **Normality:** with $n=16$ this matters. Real screen time is often skewed, so always look at the data first. Here we assume a normal population.
:::

    pic.innerHTML = g;
  }
  function draw() {
    var r = picked ? picked[0] : R15, c = picked ? picked[1] : col, s = picked ? 3 : step;
    tab.querySelectorAll("td.v, td.df").forEach(function (td) {
      var i = +td.dataset.r, j = +td.dataset.c;
      td.classList.toggle("hi", (s >= 1 && i === r) || (s >= 2 && j === c));
      td.classList.toggle("hit", s >= 3 && i === r && j === c);
    });
    tab.querySelectorAll("th[data-c]").forEach(function (th) { th.classList.toggle("sel", s >= 2 && +th.dataset.c === c); });
    var a = A[c - 1], conf = Math.round(100 - 200 * a), df = ROWS[r][0], val = ROWS[r][c];
    var t = '<b>We need</b> t with area α/2 to its right.';
    if (s >= 1) t += '<br><b>1. Row:</b> degrees of freedom' + (df === "15" ? ', n − 1 = 16 − 1 = <b>15</b>.' : ' = <b>' + df + '</b>.');
    if (s >= 2) t += '<br><b>2. Column:</b> a ' + conf + '% interval leaves ' + (100 - conf) + '% outside, split in two tails: α/2 = <b>' + a + '</b>.';
    if (s >= 3) t += '<br><b>3. Where they cross:</b> t<sub>' + a + ', ' + df + '</sub> = <b style="color:#dd6b20">' + val + '</b>';
    out.innerHTML = t;
    curve(+val, +a, s >= 3);
    btns.forEach(function (b) { b.classList.toggle("on", !picked && +b.dataset.c === col || !!picked && +b.dataset.c === picked[1] && picked[0] === R15); });
  }
  btns.forEach(function (b) { b.addEventListener("click", function () { col = +b.dataset.c; picked = null; step = 3; Reveal.navigateFragment(2); b.blur(); draw(); }); });
  tab.addEventListener("click", function (e) { var td = e.target.closest("td.v"); if (!td) return; picked = [+td.dataset.r, +td.dataset.c]; draw(); });
  function setup() {
    var sec = tab.closest("section");
    function sync() { var k = sec.querySelectorAll("span.fragment.visible").length; if (k !== step) { step = k; picked = null; draw(); } }
    Reveal.on("fragmentshown", sync); Reveal.on("fragmenthidden", sync); Reveal.on("slidechanged", sync); sync();
  }
  draw();
  if (window.Reveal && Reveal.isReady && Reveal.isReady()) setup(); else document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function () { Reveal.on("ready", setup); });
})();
</script>

## Step 3: Our 95% confidence interval

::: {.box}
$\bar{X}=170,\quad SE=10,\quad df=15,\quad t_{0.025,\,15}=2.131$
:::

. . .

::: {.box .key .c}
$$170\pm 2.131\times 10 = 170\pm 21.31$$
$$[148.69,\ 191.31]$$
:::

. . .

::: {.box .good}
We are **95% confident** that the mean daily YouTube time is between about 149 and 191 minutes.
:::

. . .

::: {.box}
<span class="tag">What "95% confident" means</span>
The **method** produces an interval containing $\mu$ in 95% of random samples. It is not a 95% probability that $\mu$ is inside this particular interval.
:::

## Step 3: Other confidence levels

| Confidence | $t_{\alpha/2,\,15}$ | Margin $t\times SE$ | Interval | Contains 150? |
|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|
| 90% | $1.753$ | $17.53$ | $[152.47,\ 187.53]$ | no |
| 95% | $2.131$ | $21.31$ | $[148.69,\ 191.31]$ | yes |
| 99% | $2.947$ | $29.47$ | $[140.53,\ 199.47]$ | yes |

. . .

::: {.box .key}
More confidence requires a **wider** interval.
:::

## Step 4: A two-sided test (theory)

::: {.box}
<span class="tag">Question</span>
Is YouTube time **different** from lecture time?
$$H_0:\ \mu=\mu_0 \qquad H_1:\ \mu\mathrel{\rlap{\,/}{=}}\mu_0$$
:::

. . .

::: {.box}
<span class="tag">Test statistic: how many SEs is $\bar{X}$ from $\mu_0$?</span>
$$t=\frac{\bar{X}-\mu_0}{s/\sqrt n}\;\sim\;t_{n-1}\quad\text{if }H_0\text{ is true}$$
:::

. . .

::: {.box .key}
<span class="tag">Decision at level $\alpha$</span>
Reject $H_0$ if $|t|>t_{\alpha/2,\,n-1}$. Equivalently, if the p-value $2\,P(T_{n-1}>|t|)$ is below $\alpha$.
:::

## Step 4: The two-sided test, our data

::: {.box}
$$H_0:\ \mu=150 \qquad H_1:\ \mu\mathrel{\rlap{\,/}{=}}150 \qquad \alpha=0.05$$
:::

. . .

::: {.box style="padding-top:0;padding-bottom:0"}
$$t=\frac{170-150}{40/\sqrt{16}}=2$$
:::

. . .

::: {.cards}
::: {.box .c}
<span class="tag">Critical value</span>
$|t|=2<2.131$
:::
::: {.box .c}
<span class="tag">P-value</span>
$p=2\,P(T_{15}\ge 2)=2\times 0.032=0.064>0.05$
:::
:::

. . .

::: {.box .warn}
**Fail to reject** $H_0$ at 5% (this does **not** show that $\mu=150$). Same answer as the interval: 150 is **inside** $[148.69,\ 191.31]$.
:::

## Step 4: The p-value

::: {.box}
**P-value:** the probability, **if $H_0$ is true**, of a statistic at least as far from $0$ as ours, in **either** direction.
$$p=P\big(|T_{n-1}|\ge |t|\big)=2\,P\big(T_{n-1}\ge |t|\big)$$
:::

<svg id="p1pv2-svg" viewBox="0 0 900 222" class="famplot" style="max-height:170px"></svg>

<script>
(function () {
  // picture of the p-value for t = 2, df = 15
  window.p1Pval = function (id, two) {
    function px(x) { return 450 + x * 95; }
    function py(x) { return 190 - 170 * Math.pow(1 + x * x / 15, -8); }
    function path(lo, hi) { var d = ""; for (var x = lo; x <= hi + 1e-9; x += 0.04) d += (d ? " L" : "M") + px(x).toFixed(1) + "," + py(x).toFixed(1); return d; }
    function area(lo, hi) { return path(lo, hi) + " L" + px(hi) + ",190 L" + px(lo) + ",190 Z"; }
    function T(x, y, str, col) { return '<text x="' + x + '" y="' + y + '" text-anchor="middle" font-size="18" font-weight="700" fill="' + col + '">' + str + '</text>'; }
    var g = '<path d="' + area(2, 4) + '" fill="#c53030" fill-opacity="0.55"/>' + T(px(2.85), 140, "area 0.032", "#c53030") + T(px(2), 213, "t = 2", "#c53030");
    if (two) g += '<path d="' + area(-4, -2) + '" fill="#c53030" fill-opacity="0.55"/>' + T(px(-2.85), 140, "area 0.032", "#c53030") + T(px(-2), 213, "−2", "#c53030");
    g += '<path d="' + path(-4, 4) + '" fill="none" stroke="#1b3a5c" stroke-width="2.5"/><line x1="60" y1="190" x2="840" y2="190" stroke="#52606d" stroke-width="1.5"/>';
    g += T(450, 213, "0", "#52606d") + T(450, 120, "t₁₅ if H₀ is true", "#1b3a5c");
    document.getElementById(id).innerHTML = g;
  };
})();
</script>

<script>window.p1Pval("p1pv2-svg", true);</script>

. . .

::: {.box}
**Table, df = 15:** $1.753<2<2.131$, so $\;0.05<p<0.10$ (two tails)
:::

. . .

::: {.box .key}
**With software:** $p=2\times 0.0320=0.064$. Reject at $\alpha=0.10$, **not** at $\alpha=0.05$ or $0.01$.
:::

## Step 5: Our real hypothesis (theory)

::: {.box}
Our suspicion was not "different". It was **more**. We stated it **before** seeing the data.
$$H_0:\ \mu=\mu_0 \qquad H_1:\ \mu>\mu_0$$
:::

. . .

::: {.box}
<span class="tag">Same test statistic</span>
$$t=\frac{\bar{X}-\mu_0}{s/\sqrt n}$$
:::

. . .

::: {.box .key}
<span class="tag">Decision at level $\alpha$</span>
Only **large** $t$ counts against $H_0$. Reject if $t>t_{\alpha,\,n-1}$, or if the p-value $P(T_{n-1}>t)$ is below $\alpha$. All of $\alpha$ is in **one** tail.
:::

## Step 5: The one-sided test, our data

::: {.box}
$$H_0:\ \mu=150 \qquad H_1:\ \mu>150 \qquad \alpha=0.05$$
:::

. . .

::: {.box}
$$t=\frac{170-150}{10}=2,\qquad t_{0.05,\,15}=1.753$$
:::

. . .

::: {.cards}
::: {.box .c}
<span class="tag">Critical value</span>
$t=2>1.753$
:::
::: {.box .c}
<span class="tag">P-value</span>
$p=P(T_{15}\ge 2)=0.032<0.05$
:::
:::

. . .

::: {.box .good}
**Reject** $H_0$: at the 5% level there is sufficient evidence that students spend on average **more than 150 minutes** a day on YouTube.
:::

. . .

::: {.box}
At $\alpha=0.01$ we would **not** reject, since $0.032>0.01$.
:::

## Step 5: The p-value

::: {.box}
For $H_1:\mu>\mu_0$ only **large** values count against $H_0$, so we take **one** tail.
$$p=P\big(T_{n-1}\ge t\big)$$
:::

<svg id="p1pv1-svg" viewBox="0 0 900 222" class="famplot" style="max-height:170px"></svg>

<script>window.p1Pval("p1pv1-svg", false);</script>

. . .

::: {.box}
**Table, df = 15:** $1.753<2<2.131$, so $\;0.025<p<0.05$
:::

. . .

::: {.box .key}
**With software:** $p=0.032$. Reject at $\alpha=0.10$ and $0.05$, **not** at $\alpha=0.01$.
:::

A **two-sided** test at level $\alpha$ rejects $\mu_0=150$ exactly when 150 is **outside** the $(1-\alpha)$ interval. Here: reject at 10%, not at 5% or 1%.
:::

## Summary: the two tests

For testing, center the picture at $\mu_0$: **which values of $\bar{X}$ make us reject $H_0$?** ($\alpha=0.05$)

<svg id="p1c-svg" viewBox="0 0 900 330" class="famplot"></svg>

<div class="readout" id="p1c-out"></div>

<div class="ctl" style="justify-content:center">
  <label>Hypothesized $\mu_0$: <input type="range" id="p1c-mu" min="135" max="205" step="0.5" value="150" style="width:420px"> <b id="p1c-val">150.0</b></label>
</div>

<script>
(function () {
  var svg = document.getElementById("p1c-svg"), sl = document.getElementById("p1c-mu"), lab = document.getElementById("p1c-val"), out = document.getElementById("p1c-out");
  var C1 = 17.53, C2 = 21.31, XB = 170, A = 100, B = 240;
  function px(v) { return 40 + (v - A) / (B - A) * 840; }
  function bar(y, lo, hi, col) { return '<rect x="' + px(lo) + '" y="' + y + '" width="' + Math.max(0, px(hi) - px(lo)) + '" height="34" fill="' + col + '"/>'; }
  function txt(x, y, s, col, anc, size) { return '<text x="' + x + '" y="' + y + '" text-anchor="' + (anc || "middle") + '" font-size="' + (size || 17) + '" font-weight="700" fill="' + col + '">' + s + '</text>'; }
  function tail(t) {   // P(T_15 > t), Simpson's rule
    var c = 0.392353, f = function (u) { return c * Math.pow(1 + u * u / 15, -8); }, a = Math.abs(t), n = 400, h = a / n, s = f(0) + f(a);
    for (var i = 1; i < n; i++) s += (i % 2 ? 4 : 2) * f(i * h);
    var q = Math.max(0, 0.5 - s * h / 3);
    return t >= 0 ? q : 1 - q;
  }
  function draw() {
    var m = +sl.value, g = "";
    lab.textContent = m.toFixed(1);
    g += txt(40, 62, "Two-sided: H₁: μ ≠ μ₀", "#1b3a5c", "start", 19);
    g += bar(74, A, m - C2, "#f4b4b4") + bar(74, m - C2, m + C2, "#cdeeda") + bar(74, m + C2, B, "#f4b4b4");
    g += txt(px(m - C2), 128, (m - C2).toFixed(2), "#c53030") + txt(px(m + C2) + 6, 128, (m + C2).toFixed(2), "#c53030", "start");
    g += txt(40, 176, "One-sided: H₁: μ > μ₀", "#1b3a5c", "start", 19);
    g += bar(188, A, m + C1, "#cdeeda") + bar(188, m + C1, B, "#f4b4b4");
    g += txt(px(m + C1) - 6, 242, (m + C1).toFixed(2), "#c53030", "end");
    g += '<line x1="40" y1="272" x2="880" y2="272" stroke="#52606d" stroke-width="2"/>';
    for (var t = 100; t <= 240; t += 20) g += '<text x="' + px(t) + '" y="292" text-anchor="middle" font-size="16" fill="#52606d">' + t + '</text>';
    g += '<line x1="' + px(m) + '" y1="68" x2="' + px(m) + '" y2="272" stroke="#2b6cb0" stroke-width="2.5" stroke-dasharray="6 5"/>' + txt(px(m), 318, "μ₀ = " + m.toFixed(1), "#2b6cb0");
    g += '<line x1="' + px(XB) + '" y1="34" x2="' + px(XB) + '" y2="272" stroke="#1f2933" stroke-width="3.5"/>' + txt(px(XB), 24, "our X̄ = 170", "#1f2933", "middle", 19);
    svg.innerHTML = g;
    var r2 = Math.abs(XB - m) > C2, r1 = XB - m > C1;
    var t = (XB - m) / 10, p1 = tail(t), p2 = 2 * tail(Math.abs(t));
    function pf(p) { return p < 0.0005 ? "p < 0.001" : p > 0.9995 ? "p > 0.999" : "p = " + p.toFixed(3); }
    out.innerHTML = 't = <b>' + t.toFixed(2) + '</b> &nbsp;·&nbsp; two-sided: <b>' + pf(p2) + '</b>, ' + (r2 ? "reject" : "fail to reject") + ' &nbsp;·&nbsp; one-sided: <b>' + pf(p1) + '</b>, ' + (r1 ? "reject" : "fail to reject") + '<br><span style="color:#2f855a;font-weight:700">green: fail to reject</span> &nbsp; <span style="color:#c53030;font-weight:700">red: reject</span> ';
  }
  sl.addEventListener("input", draw); draw();
})();
</script>

## The reveal: the population

The data were generated by a computer from this population: $X\sim N(\mu=165,\ \sigma=45)$.

::: {.fragment data-fragment-index="1"}
::: {.cap}
The dots are our 16 students. The computer draw was then adjusted by a few minutes per student (at most about 4) to make $\bar{X}=170$ and $s=40$ exact.
:::
:::

  g += '<line x1="' + px(165) + '" y1="' + py(210) + '" x2="' + px(210) + '" y2="' + py(210) + '" stroke="#1b3a5c" stroke-width="3"/><text x="' + (px(210) + 14) + '" y="' + (py(210) + 4) + '" font-size="19" font-weight="700" fill="#1b3a5c">σ = 45</text>';

## Sample vs. population

| | Population (truth) | Our sample (estimate) | Difference |
|:--|:-:|:-:|:-:|
| Mean | $\mu=165$ | $\bar{X}=170$ | $+5$ |
| Standard deviation | $\sigma=45$ | $s=40$ | $-5$ |
| Standard error of the mean | $\sigma/\sqrt{16}=11.25$ | $s/\sqrt{16}=10$ | $-1.25$ |

. . .

::: {.box}
<span class="tag">They differ, as expected. Were we lucky?</span>
$$\text{our miss in true standard errors:}\quad\frac{\bar{X}-\mu}{\sigma/\sqrt n}=\frac{170-165}{11.25}\approx 0.44$$
:::

. . .

::: {.box .good}
$P\big(|\bar{X}-\mu|>5\big)=P(|Z|>0.44)\approx 0.66$: about **two samples in three** miss $\mu$ by more than ours did. A rather good draw, not an unusual one.
:::

## Were we right?

::: {style="font-size:0.92em"}
| Our conclusion | Truth: $\mu=165$ | Verdict |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Best guess $170$ | $165$ | off by 5 minutes |
| 90% CI $[152.47,\ 187.53]$ | contains $165$ | correct |
| 95% CI $[148.69,\ 191.31]$ | contains $165$ | correct |
| 99% CI $[140.53,\ 199.47]$ | contains $165$ | correct |
| Two-sided test, 5%: $p=0.064$, fail to reject | $H_0:\mu=150$ is **false** | missed it |
| One-sided test, 5%: $p=0.032$, reject | $H_0:\mu=150$ is **false** | correct |
:::

. . .

::: {.box .key}
The two-sided test missed a difference that **really exists**. In real research $\mu$ is never revealed: we only know how reliable the **method** is.
:::

<script>
(function () {
  var N = 16, M = 100, MU0 = 150, SIG = 45, SEED = 2026;
  var T = [1.753, 2.131, 2.947], LEV = [90, 95, 99];
  var S = { mu: 165, ci: 1, test: 1 }, shown, all, rnd, timer = null;
  var svg = document.getElementById("p1e-svg"), out = document.getElementById("p1e-out");
  function mulberry32(a) { return function () { a |= 0; a = a + 0x6D2B79F5 | 0; var t = Math.imul(a ^ a >>> 15, 1 | a); t = t + Math.imul(t ^ t >>> 7, 61 | t) ^ t; return ((t ^ t >>> 14) >>> 0) / 4294967296; }; }
  function gauss() { var u = 1 - rnd(), v = rnd(); return Math.sqrt(-2 * Math.log(u)) * Math.cos(2 * Math.PI * v); }
  function one() {
    var x = [], m = 0, q = 0, i;
    for (i = 0; i < N; i++) { x.push(S.mu + SIG * gauss()); m += x[i]; }
    m /= N; for (i = 0; i < N; i++) q += (x[i] - m) * (x[i] - m);
    return { m: m, se: Math.sqrt(q / (N - 1) / N) };
  }
  function hit(o) { return Math.abs(o.m - S.mu) <= T[S.ci] * o.se; }
  function rej(o) { var t = (o.m - MU0) / o.se; return S.test === 1 ? t > 1.753 : Math.abs(t) > 2.131; }
  function add(k, keep) { for (var i = 0; i < k; i++) { var o = one(); all.push(o); if (keep && shown.length < M) shown.push(o); } }
  function stop() { if (timer) clearInterval(timer); timer = null; }
  function reset() { stop(); rnd = mulberry32(SEED + S.mu); shown = []; all = []; draw(); }
  function py(v) { return 12 + (245 - v) / 150 * 270; }
  function px(i) { return 62 + i * 8.25; }
  function draw() {
    var g = '<rect x="52" y="8" width="840" height="278" rx="8" fill="#f5f7fa"/>';
    for (var v = 100; v <= 240; v += 20) g += '<text x="46" y="' + (py(v) + 5) + '" text-anchor="end" font-size="14" fill="#7b8794">' + v + '</text>';
    shown.forEach(function (o, i) {
      var c = hit(o) ? "#2b6cb0" : "#c53030", lo = Math.max(95, o.m - T[S.ci] * o.se), hi = Math.min(245, o.m + T[S.ci] * o.se);
      g += '<line x1="' + px(i) + '" y1="' + py(hi) + '" x2="' + px(i) + '" y2="' + py(lo) + '" stroke="' + c + '" stroke-width="' + (hit(o) ? 3 : 4.5) + '"/><circle cx="' + px(i) + '" cy="' + py(o.m) + '" r="2.6" fill="#1f2933"/>';
      g += '<rect x="' + (px(i) - 3.2) + '" y="306" width="6.4" height="20" fill="' + (rej(o) ? "#1f2933" : "#d9e2ec") + '"/>';
    });
    g += '<line x1="52" y1="' + py(S.mu) + '" x2="892" y2="' + py(S.mu) + '" stroke="#dd6b20" stroke-width="3"/>';
    if (S.mu !== MU0) g += '<line x1="52" y1="' + py(MU0) + '" x2="892" y2="' + py(MU0) + '" stroke="#52606d" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="7 5"/>';
    g += '<text x="888" y="' + (py(S.mu) - 6) + '" text-anchor="end" font-size="16" font-weight="700" fill="#dd6b20" stroke="#f5f7fa" stroke-width="4" paint-order="stroke">true μ = ' + S.mu + '</text>';
    if (S.mu !== MU0) g += '<text x="888" y="' + (py(MU0) + 18) + '" text-anchor="end" font-size="16" font-weight="700" fill="#52606d" stroke="#f5f7fa" stroke-width="4" paint-order="stroke">μ₀ = 150</text>';
    g += '<text x="46" y="321" text-anchor="end" font-size="13" font-weight="700" fill="#1f2933">reject?</text>';
    g += '<text x="62" y="350" font-size="15" fill="#52606d">each column is one new sample of 16 students → &#160;&#160; bottom row: dark = reject H₀: μ = 150, light = fail to reject</text>';
    svg.innerHTML = g;
    var n = all.length;
    if (!n) { out.innerHTML = "Press a button to draw samples."; return; }
    var h = all.filter(hit).length, r = all.filter(rej).length, h0 = S.mu === MU0;
    function pc(k) { return (100 * k / n).toFixed(n > 100 ? 1 : 0) + "%"; }
    out.innerHTML = '<b>' + n.toLocaleString("en-US") + ' samples</b> &nbsp;·&nbsp; ' + LEV[S.ci] + '% CI contains μ: <b style="color:#2b6cb0">' + h.toLocaleString("en-US") + ' (' + pc(h) + ')</b>, misses: <b style="color:#c53030">' + (n - h).toLocaleString("en-US") + '</b><br>' +
      'H₀: μ = 150 is <b>' + (h0 ? "true" : "false") + '</b> (true μ = ' + S.mu + ') &nbsp;·&nbsp; rejected: <b>' + pc(r) + '</b> (' + (h0 ? "wrong" : "correct") + ') &nbsp;·&nbsp; not rejected: <b>' + pc(n - r) + '</b> (' + (h0 ? "correct" : "wrong") + ')';
  }
  function seg(id, key) {
    var box = document.getElementById(id);
    box.querySelectorAll("button").forEach(function (b) {
      b.addEventListener("click", function () {
        box.querySelectorAll("button").forEach(function (c) { c.classList.toggle("on", c === b); });
        S[key] = +b.getAttribute("data-v"); if (key === "mu") reset(); else draw();
      });
    });
  }
  seg("p1e-mu", "mu"); seg("p1e-ci", "ci"); seg("p1e-test", "test");
  document.getElementById("p1e-one").addEventListener("click", function () { stop(); add(1, true); draw(); });
  document.getElementById("p1e-all").addEventListener("click", function () {
    stop(); if (shown.length >= M) return;
    timer = setInterval(function () { add(Math.min(2, M - shown.length), true); draw(); if (shown.length >= M) stop(); }, 60);
  });
  document.getElementById("p1e-more").addEventListener("click", function () { stop(); add(10000, true); draw(); });
  document.getElementById("p1e-reset").addEventListener("click", reset);
  reset();
})();
</script>

## Why do we miss so often?

If $\sigma=45$ were **known**, we would reject when $\bar{X}>150+1.645\cdot 45/\sqrt n$.

<svg id="p1w-svg" viewBox="0 0 900 300" class="famplot" style="max-height:270px"></svg>

<div class="readout" id="p1w-out" style="color:#1f2933;min-height:1.4em"></div>

<div class="ctl" style="justify-content:center">
  <label>Sample size $n$: <input type="range" id="p1w-n" min="16" max="100" step="1" value="16" style="width:380px"> <b id="p1w-val">16</b></label>
</div>

. . .

::: {.box .key style="font-size:0.85em"}
With $n=16$ we need $\bar{X}>168.5$, **above the true mean 165**, so most samples fall short. A larger $n$ makes both curves narrower and moves the cutoff down.
:::

<script>
(function () {
  var svg = document.getElementById("p1w-svg"), sl = document.getElementById("p1w-n"), lab = document.getElementById("p1w-val"), out = document.getElementById("p1w-out");
  function Phi(z) { var x = Math.abs(z) / Math.SQRT2, t = 1 / (1 + 0.3275911 * x);
    var e = 1 - (((((1.061405429 * t - 1.453152027) * t) + 1.421413741) * t - 0.284496736) * t + 0.254829592) * t * Math.exp(-x * x);
    return z < 0 ? (1 - e) / 2 : (1 + e) / 2; }
  var A = 110, B = 205;
  function px(v) { return 40 + (v - A) / (B - A) * 840; }
  function draw() {
    var n = +sl.value, se = 45 / Math.sqrt(n), c = 150 + 1.6449 * se, pow = 1 - Phi((c - 165) / se);
    lab.textContent = n;
    var peak = 195 * Math.sqrt(n) / 10;                      // curve height grows as the curves narrow
    function py(v, m) { return 250 - Math.max(peak, 78 + peak * 0.6) * Math.exp(-0.5 * Math.pow((v - m) / se, 2)); }
    function path(m, lo, hi) { var d = "", v; for (v = lo; v < hi; v += 0.25) d += (d ? " L" : "M") + px(v).toFixed(1) + "," + py(v, m).toFixed(1); return d + " L" + px(hi).toFixed(1) + "," + py(hi, m).toFixed(1); }
    function area(m, lo, hi) { return path(m, lo, hi) + " L" + px(hi) + ",250 L" + px(lo) + ",250 Z"; }
    function T(x, y, str, col, anc, size) { return '<text x="' + x + '" y="' + y + '" text-anchor="' + (anc || "middle") + '" font-size="' + (size || 17) + '" font-weight="700" fill="' + col + '" stroke="#fff" stroke-width="4" paint-order="stroke">' + str + '</text>'; }
    var g = '<path d="' + area(165, c, B) + '" fill="#dd6b20" fill-opacity="0.35"/><path d="' + area(150, c, B) + '" fill="#52606d" fill-opacity="0.55"/>';
    g += '<path d="' + path(150, A, B) + '" fill="none" stroke="#52606d" stroke-width="2.5" stroke-dasharray="7 5"/><path d="' + path(165, A, B) + '" fill="none" stroke="#dd6b20" stroke-width="3"/>';
    g += '<line x1="40" y1="250" x2="880" y2="250" stroke="#52606d" stroke-width="1.5"/>';
    for (var t = 120; t <= 200; t += 10) g += '<text x="' + px(t) + '" y="270" text-anchor="middle" font-size="15" fill="#52606d">' + t + '</text>';
    g += T(880, 293, "sample mean X̄", "#52606d", "end", 15);
    g += '<line x1="' + px(c) + '" y1="22" x2="' + px(c) + '" y2="250" stroke="#c53030" stroke-width="3"/>' + T(px(c) + 8, 34, "reject if X̄ > " + c.toFixed(1), "#c53030", "start");
    g += '<line x1="' + px(165) + '" y1="250" x2="' + px(165) + '" y2="' + py(165, 165) + '" stroke="#dd6b20" stroke-width="1.5"/>';
    g += T(40, 34, "dashed: where X̄ falls if μ = 150 (H₀)", "#52606d", "start", 16);
    g += T(40, 58, "orange: where X̄ falls in truth, μ = 165", "#dd6b20", "start", 16);
    svg.innerHTML = g;
    out.innerHTML = '<b style="color:#dd6b20">Reject, correctly: ' + Math.round(100 * pow) + '%</b> &nbsp;·&nbsp; miss: ' + (100 - Math.round(100 * pow)) + '% &nbsp;·&nbsp; <span style="color:#52606d">false rejection if μ = 150 (dark area): 5%</span>';
  }
  sl.addEventListener("input", draw); draw();
})();
</script>

::: {.cap}
Our t-test must also estimate $\sigma$, so at $n=16$ it rejects a bit less often: about 36% instead of 38%.
:::

## What did we learn?

| In the long run, with $n=16$ | One-sided test, 5% | Two-sided test, 5% |
|:--|:-:|:-:|
| $\mu=150$ ($H_0$ true): rejects, **wrongly** | 5% | 5% |
| $\mu=165$ ($H_0$ false): rejects, **correctly** | about 36% | about 24% |

. . .

::: {.box .good}
The 95% confidence interval contains the true $\mu$ in 95% of samples, whatever $\mu$ is.
:::

. . .

::: {.box .warn}
<span class="tag">A small sample can easily miss a real difference</span>
The true gap is 15 minutes, yet the one-sided test misses it about **2 times in 3**. We rejected partly because our $\bar{X}$ landed above $\mu$.
:::

. . .

::: {.box .key}
Choose $H_1$ **before** seeing the data. "Fail to reject" is not "no difference".
:::
